items.title: Formally verifying agent-written full-stack web apps with PDD Kit
items.summary:
AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line.

items.title: Let AI do the research. Never let it form your point of view.
items.summary: ◆ The Take: For his new long-form show How We Got Here, NLW has AI read everything on a topic and generate reports of every length across several models. He uses those to build or challenge his own view. His proof that AI can't own your perspective: ask it to steelman two opposing positions and it argues each with apparent deepest conviction. It has no perspective, only the sum of the available arguments.

items.title: Two more reasons this is hard to copy
items.summary: ◆ The Take: First, a system like this is hard enough to build from scratch. If the host were replicating it, he would start a new division or product rather than retrofit an old one. Second, Spawn's self-healing depends on users' agents reporting bugs in real time, a feedback loop most products don't naturally have. The open question is whether you can design one in.
